question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{30}$ be a random sample of size $n=30$ from a population with probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}, & 0\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.33,$ calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}<1.07).$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.5\,$ | $\,0.7088\,$ | $\,0.7123\,$ | $\,0.7157\,$ |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7422\,$ | $\,0.7454\,$ | $\,0.7486\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7734\,$ | $\,0.7764\,$ | $\,0.7794\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =30,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{4}-0 \\  & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.33.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(1,\frac{0.33}{30}) \\  & ∼N(1,0.011).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<1.07).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<1.07) & =P(Z<\frac{1.07-1}{\sqrt{0.011}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<0.67) \\  & =Φ(0.67)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.67)=0.7486.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<1.07) & =Φ(1.07) \\  & =0.7486.\end{aligned}
$$
